faqs.answer: A variable is like a container for storing data. Think of it like a labeled box where you can put numbers, text, or other information so you can use it later in your code!
In Python, you use the `print()` function to display text on the screen. For example: `print("Hello, World!")` will display the text Hello, World!.
A SyntaxError means there's a typo in your code. Check for missing quotes around text, missing parentheses `()`, or forgetting a colon `:` at the end of an `if` or `for` statement.

Python uses spaces at the start of a line to know which code belongs together (like inside an `if` statement or a function). Make sure you are using 4 spaces to indent, and that all lines in the same block line up exactly!
A NameError happens when Python doesn't recognize a word you used. Usually, this means you misspelled a variable name, or you are trying to use a variable before you assigned anything to it.

A TypeError happens when you try to do something with the wrong type of data. For example, you can't add a string (text) and an integer (number) together directly. You might need to use `str()` to convert the number to text first!
A list in Python is a way to store multiple items in a single variable. It's written with square brackets. Example: `my_list = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]`.
Loops let you repeat code. A `for` loop is great when you know how many times to repeat something (like going through a list). A `while` loop repeats as long as a condition is true.
If statements let your code make decisions. `if` checks a condition. If it's true, it runs the code inside. `elif` (else if) checks another condition. `else` runs if none of the above were true.
A function is a reusable block of code. You define it using `def my_function():`, and then you can call it whenever you need that code to run by typing `my_function()`.
SQL (Structured Query Language) is used to talk to databases. You can use it to SELECT data, INSERT new data, UPDATE existing data, or DELETE data.
The SELECT statement in SQL is used to get data from a database. For example: `SELECT * FROM users;` gets all columns from the users table.
